searches.query: trigger auth.users update function not working
trigger function on auth.users update not firing

When you update a row in auth.users, the trigger that calls your function to sync public.users does not fire because triggers on auth.users only run for INSERT, or because the function lacks security definer / search_path permissions.

input.intent: User's custom function/trigger tied to auth.users updates isn't working - find Supabase docs explaining limitations or requirements for triggers/functions on auth.users table

[Resource from qmd at qmd://supabase/apps/docs/content/guides/auth/managing-user-data.mdx] 1: ---
2: id: 'user-management'
3: title: 'User Management'
4: subtitle: 'View, delete, and export user information.'
5: ---
6: 
7: You can view your users on the [Users page](/dashboard/project/_/auth/users) of the Dashboard. You can also view the contents of the Auth schema in the [Table Editor](/dashboard/project/_/editor).
8: 
9: ## Accessing user data via API
10: 
11: For security, the Auth schema is not exposed in the auto-generated API. If you want to access users data via the API, you can create your own user tables in the `public` schema.
12: 
13: Make sure to protect the table by enabling [Row Level Security](/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security) and only granting the necessary privileges for each role. Reference the `auth.users` table to ensure data integrity. Specify `on delete cascade` in the reference. For example, a `public.profiles` table might look like this:
14: 
15: ```sql
16: create table public.profiles (
17:   id uuid not null references auth.users on delete cascade,
18:   first_name text,
19:   last_name text,
20: 
21:   primary key (id)
22: );
23: 
24: -- Grant the privileges the roles need
25: GRANT SELECT ON public.profiles TO anon;
26: GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON public.profiles TO authenticated;
27: GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON public.profiles TO service_role;
28: 
29: -- Enable row level security for the table
30: alter table public.profiles enable row level security;
31: ```
32: 
33: <Admonition type="caution">
34: 
35: Only use primary keys as [foreign key references](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/tutorial-fk.html) for schemas and tables like `auth.users` which are managed by Supabase. Postgres lets you specify a foreign key reference for columns backed by a unique index (not necessarily primary keys).
36: 
37: Primary keys are **guaranteed not to change**. Columns, indices, constraints or other database objects managed by Supabase **may change at any time** and you should be careful when referencing them directly.
38: 
39: </Admonition>
40: 
41: To update your `public.profiles` table every time a user signs up, set up a trigger. If the trigger fails, it could block signups, so test your code thoroughly.
42: 
43: ```sql
44: -- inserts a row into public.profiles
45: create function public.handle_new_user()
46: returns trigger
47: language plpgsql
48: security definer set search_path = ''
49: as $$
50: begin
51:   insert into public.profiles (id, first_name, last_name)
52:   values (new.id, new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'first_name', new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'last_name');
53:   return new;
54: end;
55: $$;
56: 
57: -- trigger the function every time a user is created
58: create trigger on_auth_user_created
59:   after insert on auth.users
60:   for each row execute procedure public.handle_new_user();
61: ```
62: 
63: ## Adding and retrieving user metadata
64: 
65: You can assign metadata to users on sign up:
66: 
67: <Tabs
68:   scrollable
69:   size="small"
70:   type="underlined"
71:   defaultActiveId="js"
72:   queryGroup="language"
73: >
74: <TabPanel id="js" label="JavaScript">
75: 
76: ```js
77: import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'
78: const supabase = createClient(process.env.SUPABASE_URL!, process.env.SUPABASE_KEY!)
79: 
80: // ---cut---

The default guide (`guides/auth/managing-user-data.mdx`, "Accessing user data via API") only sets up a trigger for `INSERT` — `on_auth_user_created` fires `after insert on auth.users`, so updates to `auth.users` never call your function.

**Fix:** add a matching `UPDATE` trigger, per `guides/database/prisma/prisma-troubleshooting.mdx` (lines 199–238):
```sql
create trigger on_auth_user_updated
  after update on auth.users
  for each row execute procedure public.update_user();
```
Also ensure your trigger function is `security definer set search_path = ''` (same doc, line 216), since missing definer rights silently blocks writes to `public` tables from an `auth.users` trigger.
